n: Luke anchors the birth of Jesus in world history. Caesar Augustus, Rome’s first emperor, ordered a registration of everyone in the empire, likely for taxation.

f.g: Octavian, first Roman emperor, ruled 27 BC-AD 14.
Enrolled, registered in a census.

n: This was the first registration under Quirinius, governor of Syria. The exact dating is debated by historians, but Luke wants readers to know this happened in real history.

f.g: The Greek form of Quirinius, a Roman official over Syria.

n: Everyone went to their ancestral hometown to register.
Joseph traveled from Nazareth in Galilee to Bethlehem in Judea — David’s hometown — because he was from David’s family line. A Roman decree put Jesus exactly where Micah prophesied he’d be born.

f.g: Hebrew “house of bread,” a village about 6 miles south of Jerusalem.

n: He went with Mary, his betrothed wife, who was far along in pregnancy. The trip of about 80-90 miles would have been hard for her.

f.g: Heavily pregnant.

n: While they were in Bethlehem, the time came for her baby to be born.

f.g: Completed, fulfilled.

n: Mary gave birth to her firstborn son, wrapped him snugly in strips of cloth, and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no space in the lodging place. The King of kings began life in humble circumstances.

f.g: Strips of cloth wrapped snugly around a newborn.
A feeding trough for animals.
Greek kataluma — a guest room or lodging place, the same word used for the “guestchamber” of the Last Supper.

n: Nearby, shepherds were living out in the fields, guarding their flocks through the night. Shepherds were humble working men, often looked down on.

f.g: Staying, living.

n: An angel of the Lord stood before them, and the Lord’s glory blazed around them. They were terrified.

f.g: Very frightened.

n: The angel said: don’t be afraid — I bring you good news of great joy for all people.
Today in David’s town a Savior has been born for you: he is Christ the Lord. Three titles in one breath: Savior, Messiah, and Lord.

f.w: a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord

n: The sign: you’ll find a baby wrapped in cloths lying in a feeding trough. A strange sign for a king — and that’s the point.
Suddenly a vast army of heavenly beings joined the angel, praising God.

f.g: The armies of heaven — a great company of angels.

n: “Glory to God in the highest heaven, and on earth peace and good will toward people.” Christ’s birth brings honor to God and peace to humankind.
When the angels left, the shepherds said: let’s go to Bethlehem and see what the Lord has told us about.
They hurried off and found Mary, Joseph, and the baby lying in the manger, just as promised.
After seeing him, they spread the word about what they had been told about this child. Humble shepherds became the first witnesses of Christ’s birth.
Everyone who heard the shepherds’ story was amazed.
But Mary treasured all these things, quietly turning them over in her heart. Pondering is a pattern for receiving deeper understanding.

f.g: Thought deeply, put things together.

n: The shepherds went back glorifying and praising God because everything was just as they had been told.
On the eighth day he was circumcised and named Jesus, the name the angel gave before his conception. His parents obeyed both the law and the angel.
After Mary’s forty days of purification under the law, they brought Jesus to the temple in Jerusalem to present him to the Lord.

f.g: A ritual cleansing after childbirth, completed with an offering.

n: The law said every firstborn son belonged to the Lord, recalling how God spared Israel’s firstborn in Egypt.

f.w: Every male that openeth the womb
f.g: Every firstborn son.

n: They offered two turtledoves or two young pigeons — the offering allowed for families too poor to afford a lamb. Jesus was born into a family of modest means.

f.w: A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons

n: In Jerusalem lived Simeon, a righteous, devout man waiting for the comfort God would bring Israel. The Holy Ghost was upon him.

f.g: The comfort and deliverance of Israel through the Messiah.

n: The Holy Ghost had revealed to him that he would not die before seeing the Lord’s Anointed.

f.g: The Lord’s Messiah, the Anointed One.

n: Prompted by the Spirit, he came into the temple courts just as Jesus’ parents brought him in to fulfill the law’s requirements. Following a spiritual prompting put him in the right place at the right moment.
Simeon took the baby in his arms and praised God.
His song, called the “Nunc Dimittis,” begins: Lord, now you can let your servant die in peace, as you promised.

f.g: Here, to die — to be released from service.

n: “My eyes have seen your salvation.” Holding the baby, Simeon held salvation itself.
God prepared this salvation in the sight of all peoples.
Jesus would be a light of revelation to the Gentiles and the glory of Israel — salvation for the whole world, not one nation only.

f.w: A light to lighten the Gentiles

n: Joseph and Mary marveled at what was said about their son.

f.g: Some ancient manuscripts read “his father and his mother.”

n: Simeon blessed them and told Mary that the child would cause many in Israel to fall and to rise. He would be a sign that people would oppose. People’s response to Jesus would reveal them.

f.w: the fall and rising again of many

n: And a sword would pierce Mary’s own soul — a prophecy of her grief at the cross. Through him the hidden thoughts of many would be exposed.

f.w: a sword shall pierce through thy own soul

n: Anna was also there, a prophetess of the tribe of Asher. She had been married only seven years before her husband died.

f.g: Asher, one of the northern tribes of Israel.

n: She was a widow of eighty-four (or a widow for eighty-four years) who never left the temple, worshipping night and day with fasting and prayer.

f.g: Eighty-four.

n: Arriving at that very moment, she thanked God and spoke about the child to everyone waiting for Jerusalem’s redemption. A woman and a man both witness of him, fulfilling the law of witnesses.

f.g: Waited in hope for God to redeem his people.

n: When they had done everything the law required, they returned home to Nazareth in Galilee. (Matthew adds the visit of the wise men and the flight to Egypt.)
The child grew strong, was filled with wisdom, and God’s grace was on him.

f.g: God’s favor and enabling power.

n: Every year Jesus’ parents traveled to Jerusalem for Passover — a sign of a faithful family.
When Jesus was twelve, they went up for the feast as usual. A Jewish boy began taking on adult religious duties around this age.
After the festival, as they headed home, Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem without his parents realizing it.

f.g: Stayed behind.

n: Assuming he was somewhere in the large traveling group, they went a full day’s journey before searching among relatives and friends.

f.g: Caravan, traveling group of families from the same area.

n: Not finding him, they returned to Jerusalem to look for him.
After three days they found him in the temple courts, sitting among the teachers, listening and asking questions. The JST says the teachers were listening to him and asking him questions.

f.g: Teachers of the law, scholars.

f.w: both hearing them, and asking them questions
f.g: JST: “and they were hearing him, and asking him questions.”

n: Everyone who heard him was astonished at his understanding and his answers.
His parents were shocked. Mary said, “Son, why have you done this to us? Your father and I have been searching for you anxiously.”

f.g: In anguish, distressed.

n: Jesus’ first recorded words: “Why were you searching? Didn’t you know I must be about my Father’s business?” Gently he pointed to his true Father, God.

f.g: Didn’t you know.
Can also be read “in my Father’s house.”

n: They didn’t understand what he meant.
He went home to Nazareth with them and was obedient to them. Mary treasured all these things in her heart.

f.g: Obedient to them.

n: Jesus grew in wisdom (mentally), stature (physically), and favor with God (spiritually) and with people (socially). A balanced pattern for growing up.
